lines.text: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW a1c_for_measure AS
CASE WHEN r.unit = 'mmol/mol' THEN round(0.09148 * r.value_num + 2.152, 1)
CASE WHEN r.unit = 'mmol/mol' THEN r.value_num / 10 ELSE r.value_num END AS a1c_pct

sources.cite: AMIA Accreditation Committee, foundational domains for master's-level health informatics education (CAHIIM HI master's curriculum requirements PDF; approved by the AMIA Board December 2016)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. The ten foundational domains F1-F10 as the MSHI course uses them; F4 (Health Information Science and Technology) covers methods, tools and standards for collecting, organizing and sharing health data: 'Systems design and development addresses standards, integration, interoperability, and protection of information.' The course's data quality objective paraphrases the dimensions named by Weiskopf and Weng (2013, JAMIA, PMC3555312); that article's page did not load through the fetch, so its definitions are marked to verify and the case defines each check in its own words.

sources.cite: eCQI Resource Center, CMS122v13, Diabetes: Glycemic Status Assessment Greater Than 9% (2025 performance period)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. Patients 18-75 with diabetes; the measure counts a glycemic status assessment above 9.0%; improvement notation 'Lower score indicates better quality'. The fetch did not show how a missing result is counted; the case's dashboard counts a patient with no result this year in the numerator, as the measure's earlier HbA1c Poor Control versions did, and says so on the screen. The case uses no measure version's exact logic.

sources.cite: NGSP, IFCC Standardization of HbA1c (master equation)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: 'NGSP = [0.09148 * IFCC] + 2.152', IFCC in mmol/mol; 6.5% is about 48 mmol/mol and 9% is 75 mmol/mol. The case's conversion is this equation.

sources.cite: LOINC 4548-4 (Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood, mass fraction, example unit %) and LOINC 59261-8 (Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood by IFCC protocol, substance fraction, example unit mmol/mol), as listed by FindACode
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through summarizing fetches of the two FindACode pages (a third-party listing, not loinc.org): 4548-4 property MFr, scale Qn, system Bld, example unit %; 59261-8 property SFr, example UCUM unit mmol/mol, and 'not proposed for use in the United States'. The point the case teaches is that the two codes carry the same analyte in different units.

sources.cite: HL7 V2-to-FHIR, ConceptMap SegmentOBXComponentToObservation, version 1.0.0 (STU1, informative)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: OBX-3 (Observation Identifier) maps to the code, OBX-5 carries the value whose type OBX-2 sets (NM to a quantity), OBX-6 carries the units for NM values, and OBX-11 is the result status. A value without its OBX-6 unit is not the whole result.
Ridgeview Community Health, Harbor Reference Lab, every person, count, rate, run time and deadline are invented teaching values, not measured ones. No patient data appears in the case.

brief.situation: You are the informatics analyst at Ridgeview Community Health (fictional). This month's diabetes dashboard says 41.2% of patients with diabetes have a latest A1c above 9%; for five months it has been about 18%. On 3 November the outpatient clinics started sending A1c tests to Harbor Reference Lab (fictional) through a new HL7 v2 results interface. The quality committee packet goes out at 15:00. It is 14:00.
handover: The dashboard reads the a1c_for_measure view, which takes the numeric result from each A1c result row.
A patient with no A1c this year counts in the numerator, as poor control.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: profile the data, read the interface messages, change the measure view, run a check, or send the dashboard. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
The console shows what is open, its flags, the trend chart, tables and the view's code, and the result of each step. 'Read the console' reads it aloud, and the chart can be shown as a table.
Sending the dashboard is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the quality director: why the rate jumped, what you changed, and how you know the new figure is right.

parts.label: Why it jumped
parts.criteria: Names the data quality failure: the new lab's A1c arrives under LOINC 59261-8 in mmol/mol (OBX-6), the view took OBX-5 as a percentage, so values like 58 failed plausibility and counted as above 9%. Not a real change in care.
parts.modelAnswer: Harbor sends IFCC mmol/mol under 59261-8; the view ignored the unit, so 64 mmol/mol (8.0%) was read as 64%.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: Converts in the measure view, keyed on the unit or code, with the NGSP equation; leaves the stored results as the lab reported them; does not drop Harbor's results (that makes 640 patients look untested, a completeness failure) and does not divide by 10.
parts.modelAnswer: a1c_pct = 0.09148 x mmol/mol + 2.152 when the unit is mmol/mol, in the view only; ticket to the interface team.

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: A check after the last change: every value plausible, and a concordance check of converted results against the lab's own reported percentages; the trend is consistent with prior months.
parts.modelAnswer: Range 4.6-15.8%; 20 of 20 sampled results match Harbor's PDF; 18.1% against 17.6% in October.

expertPath.text: Profile A1c by lab: Harbor's median is 58, maximum 112; impossible as %.
Read Harbor's messages: LOINC 59261-8, OBX-6 mmol/mol.
Convert in the view by unit: 0.09148 x mmol/mol + 2.152. Rate 18.1%.
Check: range 4.6-15.8%, 20 of 20 sampled results match Harbor's reports.
Ticket to the interface team; send the dashboard.

right.headline: Good: plausibility, then concordance
right.body: A1c of 58% cannot exist, so the jump was a data problem. The codes and units showed which one, the conversion went in the view and not the record, and a check against the lab's own reports proved it.

gaps.headline: Sent, with gaps
gaps.body: The rate is right; it went late, or without a check after the last change to prove it.

wrongSent.headline: A wrong rate went out
wrongSent.body: A rate that moves 23 points in a month is a data quality signal before it is a clinical one. Profile the values and read the units before you report.

altered.headline: The record was changed to fix a report
altered.body: Stored results are what the lab reported and part of the legal record. Convert in the reporting layer, keyed on the unit, and have the interface fixed at the source.

notSent.headline: Nothing sent
notSent.body: Safe, but the committee needed the figure, and the conversion is one line in the view.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was recorded before the case's limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: A rate that more than doubles in a month, coinciding with a new lab interface, is a data quality question first. Plausibility: an A1c median of 58 and maximum of 112 cannot be percentages. Concordance with the message: OBX-3 is LOINC 59261-8 and OBX-6 is mmol/mol, the IFCC unit, while the view assumed %. Convert in the measure view with the NGSP master equation, keyed on the unit, so the stored results stay as the lab reported them. Leaving Harbor out would make 640 patients look untested, which the measure counts as poor control; dividing by 10 is not the conversion. Then check: every value plausible, sampled results match the lab's own reports, and 18.1% sits with prior months. Ask the interface team to review the mapping so other reports are right too.
